```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(eval = FALSE, collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

Query a SQL warehouse with DBI or call brickster functions using the
visitor's Databricks account. Start with a query; add workspace API calls
when your app needs them.

## Register the app

Install `brickster`. Ask your Databricks administrator to
[register a custom OAuth application](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/integrations/enable-disable-oauth)
with `http://localhost:8100` as a redirect URI. Allow the scopes requested
by the client preset, including `all-apis` and `offline_access`. Users need
access to the workspace, SQL warehouse, and queried data.

Put your registration's values in a local `.Renviron` file and restart R:

```text
OAUTHDB_CLIENT_ID=your-client-id
OAUTHDB_CLIENT_SECRET=your-client-secret
```

This example uses a confidential OAuth app with a client secret. For a public
registration, omit `client_secret`. Find the SQL warehouse ID in the
warehouse's connection details.

## A complete app

Save this as `app.R` and replace the example connection settings:

```{r app}
library(shiny)
library(shinyOAuth)
library(shinyOAuthDB)

host <- "example.cloud.databricks.com"
client <- oauth_db_databricks_client(
  host = host,
  client_id = Sys.getenv("OAUTHDB_CLIENT_ID"),
  client_secret = Sys.getenv("OAUTHDB_CLIENT_SECRET"),
  redirect_uri = "http://localhost:8100"
)

ui <- oauth_ui(fluidPage(
  actionButton("login", "Sign in"),
  actionButton("logout", "Sign out"),
  tableOutput("rows")
), id = "auth", client = client)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  auth <- oauth_module_server("auth", client, auto_redirect = FALSE)
  observeEvent(input$login, auth$request_login())
  observeEvent(input$logout, auth$logout())

  con <- oauth_db_databricks(
    auth$connection,
    host = host,
    warehouse_id = "warehouse-id"
  )

  output$rows <- renderTable({
    connection <- con()
    DBI::dbGetQuery(connection, "SELECT current_user()")
  })
}

shinyApp(ui, server, options = list(port = 8100), uiPattern = ".*")
```

Run `shiny::runApp(port = 8100)` in that directory, then open
`http://localhost:8100` and sign in. The output waits for sign-in and clears
when you sign out.

The query shows the Databricks user. Replace it with SQL for your tables.
For dbplyr, obtain `connection <- con()` first, then pass `connection` to
`dplyr::tbl()`.

## Call brickster functions

Keep the same sign-in client. Add `verbatimTextOutput("warehouses")` to
the UI and this code inside `server()`:

```{r warehouses}
databricks <- oauth_db_databricks_api(auth$connection, host = host)

output$warehouses <- renderPrint({
  databricks$call(brickster::db_sql_warehouse_list)
})
```

Pass the function's usual arguments to `$call()`. The client supplies the
workspace host and visitor's current token. For example, brickster's query
API can replace the DBI output:

```{r api-query}
output$rows <- renderPrint({
  databricks$call(
    brickster::db_sql_query,
    warehouse_id = "warehouse-id",
    statement = "SELECT current_user()",
    disposition = "INLINE",
    show_progress = FALSE
  )
})
```

Use `verbatimTextOutput("rows")` for this alternative, which keeps
brickster's native return value. Use the DBI helper when you want a data frame
from `DBI::dbGetQuery()`.

## Azure Databricks with Entra sign-in

If your workspace uses Microsoft Entra tokens, replace the sign-in client
with:

```{r entra-client}
client <- oauth_db_microsoft_client(
  services = "databricks_entra",
  tenant_id = Sys.getenv("OAUTHDB_TENANT_ID"),
  client_id = Sys.getenv("OAUTHDB_CLIENT_ID"),
  client_secret = Sys.getenv("OAUTHDB_CLIENT_SECRET"),
  redirect_uri = "http://localhost:8100"
)
```

Use an Entra Web registration with the appropriate delegated Databricks
permission, and set `OAUTHDB_TENANT_ID`. Replace `host` with your Azure
workspace hostname and set `auth_mode = "entra"` on both
`oauth_db_databricks()` and `oauth_db_databricks_api()`.

## Connection options

Supply `http_path = "/sql/1.0/warehouses/warehouse-id"` instead of
`warehouse_id` if you prefer. Optional `catalog` and `schema` arguments
set the SQL defaults. Other connection options go to brickster.

Call `con()` before each operation. The helper replaces the DBI handle when
its token changes and closes it on sign-out or session end. For results you
store in the app, see [Authentication and sessions](authorization.html).
